events.title: King James I of Scotland is murdered at Perth
events.description: James I, King of Scots since 1406, was murdered at Perth in a failed coup by his uncle and former ally Walter Stewart, Earl of Atholl. Atholl was tried for the murder and executed.
events.html: James I, King of Scots since 1406, was murdered at Perth in a failed coup by his uncle and former ally Walter Stewart, Earl of Atholl. Atholl was tried for the murder and executed.

events.title: Mikhail Romanov elected Tsar of Russia
events.description: An assembly of the land chose sixteen-year-old Mikhail Romanov as tsar (21 February Old Style), ending the Time of Troubles. His dynasty ruled Russia until the revolution of 1917.
events.html: An assembly of the land chose sixteen-year-old Mikhail Romanov as tsar (21 February Old Style), ending the Time of Troubles. His dynasty ruled Russia until the revolution of 1917.

events.title: The Crown garrison at Inverness surrenders to the Jacobite army
events.description: After three days of fighting, Crown forces holding Old Fort George, a medieval castle at Inverness, surrendered to the supporters of Charles Edward Stuart, who had threatened to blow up the castle by tunnelling under its walls.
events.html: After three days of fighting, Crown forces holding Old Fort George, a medieval castle at Inverness, surrendered to the supporters of Charles Edward Stuart, who had threatened to blow up the castle by tunnelling under its walls.

events.title: Trevithick's steam locomotive makes the first railway journey
events.description: Richard Trevithick's locomotive hauled ten tons of iron and some 70 men along the Penydarren tramway in South Wales. It was the first working railway journey by a steam locomotive.
events.html: Richard Trevithick's locomotive hauled ten tons of iron and some 70 men along the Penydarren tramway in South Wales. It was the first working railway journey by a steam locomotive.

events.title: Marx and Engels publish 'The Communist Manifesto'
events.description: Commissioned by the Communist League, the pamphlet appeared in German in London just as revolution swept Europe. Its call 'Workers of the world, unite!' inspired socialist movements for generations.
events.html: Commissioned by the Communist League, the pamphlet appeared in German in London just as revolution swept Europe. Its call 'Workers of the world, unite!' inspired socialist movements for generations.

events.title: Battle of Verdun begins
events.description: After a massive bombardment, the German army attacked the French fortress city of Verdun. The battle lasted ten months and caused some 700,000 casualties, becoming a symbol of French endurance.

events.title: Malcolm X assassinated in Harlem
events.description: Malcolm X was shot dead as he began speaking at the Audubon Ballroom in New York. A year after leaving the Nation of Islam, he had been moving towards a broader vision of human rights.
events.html: Malcolm X was shot dead as he began speaking at the Audubon Ballroom in New York. A year after leaving the Nation of Islam, he had been moving towards a broader vision of human rights.

events.title: Richard Nixon arrives in Beijing
events.description: Nixon became the first US President to visit the People's Republic of China, meeting Mao Zedong. His week-long trip ended more than two decades of hostility and reshaped Cold War diplomacy.
